messages:
sam-sales: Heads up 2 FinServX POC. Theyre behind a corporate proxy that performs TLS interception. Our Node + Python SDKs intermittently get 502/504 and occasional 429s during streaming. Need help triaging and also a quick pricing/SOW note.

rachel-se: Can you share minimal reproducer logs and whether it's affecting non-stream endpoints (health/status) or only streaming/generate?

sam-sales: Only streaming seems flaky; simple /v1/health works usually but long-lived streaming connections drop mid-stream. They attached a Python stacktrace: `socket.timeout: The read operation timed out` and node shows `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` when routed via proxy.

devin-eng: Common pattern: proxy is re-signing TLS and either closing/rotating pooled sockets or not handling HTTP/2 ALPN well. Quick diagnostics: have them run curl with `--verbose --http1.1 -x http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` and set DEBUG env for our SDKs (`REDWOOD_DEBUG=1`).

nate-platform: Short-term mitigations Id suggest: (1) disable client connection pooling / keepalive so proxy doesn't recycle sockets, (2) force HTTP/1.1 to avoid HTTP/2 downgrade issues, (3) increase streaming timeout to 60-90s and add jittered exponential backoff for retries to prevent surge. For Node you can do: `new Agent({ keepAlive: false })` or set `agent: false` in fetch. For Python requests, create a new Session per call or mount an adapter with `pool_maxsize=1` and `pool_block=True`.

rachel-se: Example Node snippet we gave the customer: `fetch(url, { agent: new https.Agent({ keepAlive: false }), timeout: 60000 })` and `fetchOptions.forceHttp1 = true` (our SDK exposes that flag). For Python: `session = requests.Session(); session.trust_env = False; adapter = HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=1, pool_maxsize=1); session.mount('https://', adapter)` then `session.get(...)`.

infra-bot: deploy: production-runtime v2.4.1 deployed 03/15 22:05 UTC  no streaming-related regressions detected.

devin-eng: If theyre still seeing 502s after client tweaks, ask them to check proxy logs for dropped/closed CONNECT tunnels and whether the appliance re-signs or renegotiates TLS mid-connection. If the proxy performs active MITM and rotates certs, long-lived TLS sessions can break. Options: (A) allow raw TLS passthrough for api.redwood.ai on their proxy, (B) terminate TLS at the proxy but ensure it preserves SNI and ALPN, or (C) place an outbound bastion with TLS passthrough.

sam-sales: They ran `curl --http1.1` and got `200` from /v1/health but streaming still sometimes aborts after ~30s. They shared proxy
logs showing repeated `CONNECT` success then `TLS alert (close_notify)` entries.

nate-platform: That's consistent with the appliance terminating and closing sessions. For the SOW/pricing: ask for token counts including retries and failed-chunk overhead. For an initial estimate we should add a 10-20% buffer to their monthly token forecast to account for retries. Maria (pricing) not in thread, but I can draft a note.

ingrid-security: On the questionnaire: we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private, logs/audit exports via S3 or SIEM forwarding, and can provide compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO). If customer proxy re-signs TLS, that's a customer-controlled risk  we provide guidance but cannot bypass their interception for security reasons. They should document acceptance in the questionnaire.

rachel-se: Can we add a Dedicated config example they can point to for longer streaming SLOs? They want to know if we can set route-level keepalive and per-connection timeouts.

devin-eng: Yes. Example fields: `route.stream.keepalive_ms: 120000`, `route.connection.max_idle_ms: 180000`, and `serve.max_stream_duration_ms: 300000`. On Dedicated we can tune those per-route and set connection pooling behavior on the runtime.

sam-sales: Customer ran with no-pooling + force HTTP/1.1 + longer timeout and streaming success rate improved significantly. They still see an occasional mid-stream drop but it recovers with client retry. They asked if we support per-route connection pinning on Dedicated to avoid proxy-induced teardown.

nate-platform: We can enable connection pinning in Dedicated for customer VPCs; that reduces reuse across different upstreams but may increase connections. We'll include that option in the Dedicated eval SOW.

ingrid-security: I'll attach the compliance pack and a short guidance doc on operating with TLS-intercepting proxies (recommendations: add exceptions for api.redwood.ai, allow SNI passthrough, or use a bastion).

sam-sales: Next steps Im tracking: (1) customer to run `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` and share logs, (2) devin to provide Dedicated config snippet and note on pinning, (3) security to share compliance artifacts, (4) I'll update SOW with a 15% retry buffer and an option for Dedicated connection pinning.

rachel-se: Customer confirmed improved stability after client-side changes. We'll leave this open until SOW signed. Thx all. :thumbsup:
